title: UI Systems Lab
summary: I’m building a UI library in Storybook and a space to explore flows with those patterns.

Owner's clarification: shared patterns, different fidelity, and what prototyping enables

sections.title: About the project
sections.body: I use Storybook to work on the library and the starter apps to try it in context. This page brings those pieces together so you can look through the UI and the code behind it.

evidence.note: The owner specified one Storybook project with Vite and TanStack explained as prototype spaces.
The README identifies packages/ui as the component, token, and Storybook catalog.

sections.title: Why I built this space
sections.body:
I wanted a place to work out design ideas in code without starting from scratch each time. With the basics ready, I can spend more time exploring how a form behaves or how someone moves through a task.

Storybook gives me a place to build and inspect those reusable pieces. The prototype workspace lets me try them in a larger flow.

evidence.note: Adapted from the retained article draft's goals: connecting design decisions to code, providing reusable UI for rapid prototyping, and focusing on flows. This states intended purpose, not measured outcomes.

sections.title: Trying a flow in context
sections.body: For a task like the create-record example above, I can sketch the steps first, then bring familiar components into a prototype to explore the interaction.

evidence.note: The owner clarified that the prototyping workspace uses the Storybook patterns at different levels of fidelity. The explanation should focus on what this enables rather than inventorying the frameworks.
The Vite README describes apps/web as a demo page, with optional area pages and no application router.
The TanStack README documents file routes in apps/web for pages and area views.

sections.title: Putting the pieces together
sections.body: In Storybook, I can move from individual controls to patterns for a complete task. This create-record example brings fields, actions, and feedback together in one place.

items.title: Foundations
items.summary: The color, type, spacing and motion choices used throughout the library.

items.title: Layout
items.summary: Page frames, overlays and ways to arrange content.

items.title: Components
items.summary: Individual controls, including buttons, fields and navigation.

items.title: Modules
items.summary: Groups of components that work together, such as forms, tables and detail views.

items.title: Patterns
items.summary: Examples of tasks such as creating a record, onboarding and managing work.

evidence.note: The README documents the Foundations, Layout, Components, Modules and Patterns Storybook groups and representative subjects.
The parallel TanStack README documents the same catalog taxonomy.

sections.title: What I’m improving next
sections.body: I want someone exploring the library to see how a component is used and what happens in different states. The next step is clearer usage notes and more code examples, then trying them in the prototype apps.

evidence.note: The retained article draft describes the goal of making the library useful to developers through component examples and clearer notes about supported behavior. These remain goals, not completed capabilities.
The owner describes the starter environments as prototype spaces in a portfolio lab.
The Vite source is a separate starter project.
The TanStack Start source is a separate starter project.

curationNotes: Rick reviewed and approved the concept for publication on October 28, 2026.
The create-record diagram is an illustration based on the Storybook source; the rough and detailed flow comparison is illustrative, not a screenshot or record of a completed study.
The Why I built this space section adapts the earlier article draft's stated goals; no historical client experience or measured benefit is implied.
The create-record Storybook story was inspected in a browser; saving changes local UI state without persisting a record.
Do not present the catalog taxonomy diagram as a screenshot or claim unverified component usage, accessibility conformance, performance, adoption, or usability outcomes.
The Vite and TanStack catalogs are parallel repositories; avoid implying one shared deployed package or synchronized codebase.
No protected client work or third-party imagery is used.
